urine human chorionic gonadotropin test was negative

concepts.why: The patient had a 15 × 6 cm cystic mass with regular margins arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex, and purulent fluid was noted upon incision of the cyst wall.
A second abdominopelvic ultrasound was interpreted as suggestive of retrocecal appendicitis.
The patient had a leukocyte count of 12,200/μL, C-reactive protein of 12 mg/L, and a cystic mass with purulent fluid arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex.
The patient had a 15 × 6 cm cystic mass with regular margins arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex, and purulent fluid was noted upon incision of the cyst wall.

The negative urine human chorionic gonadotropin test helps to rule out ectopic pregnancy, but given the clinical presentation, it is still a consideration that needs to be evaluated in the context of the patient's symptoms and other test results.

The negative HIV testing is important in the context of considering pelvic tuberculosis, as immunocompromised states can increase the risk of tuberculosis, and the patient's symptoms and ultrasound findings could be consistent with a tubercular infection.

rationales.F01: Nausea, vomiting, and right lower-quadrant abdominal pain are non-specific symptoms.
rationales.F04: Tender right lower abdominal quadrant is a common symptom of various conditions.
rationales.F11: A 15 × 6 cm cystic mass with regular margins arising from the right tubo-ovarian complex is highly suggestive of a right tubo-ovarian abscess or ovarian cyst infection.
rationales.F12: Purulent fluid noted in the cyst is highly suggestive of an infectious process, such as a right tubo-ovarian abscess or ovarian cyst infection.
